Description: The entry phase where price aligns with the higher timeframe direction after the correction has been cleaned up.
Indication/Entry Rules: Wait for price to flip back in the original direction, breaking the 15M / 5M structure (lower high in a downtrend or higher low in an uptrend).
Stop Loss Placement: Placed below the previous level of support/resistance or the higher low/lower high created during the correction.
Targeting Strategy: Initially target the previous 1H / 4H swing high or low. Can be held for longer trends if higher timeframe structure remains intact.
Analogy/Psychology: The surgeon analogy: The 1H is the outside view; you must 'go inside' the lower timeframes (X-ray) to see the real cause/reversal before operating.

Description: The first step of the model representing the initial breakout and explosion, signaling market intent.
Indication/Entry Rules: Price breaks above a previous swing high or below a previous swing low. This is treated as information, not an entry signal.
Targeting Strategy: Defines the potential targets for the eventual trade based on the peak of the breakout move.
Analogy/Psychology: Coke bottle analogy: Shaking the bottle builds pressure (consolidation), and the explosion (indication) is when the cap flies off.

Description: A calculated market pause or reversal designed to trap emotional breakout and FOMO traders to grab liquidity.
Indication/Entry Rules: Occurs after the new high or new low is created. Traders must switch to the 15-minute chart to monitor this phase.
Targeting Strategy: Used to find a deeper entry point before the trend continues.
Analogy/Psychology: The 'mess' after the Coke bottle explosion. It shakes out weak hands and late FOMO traders to fuel the sustainable trend.
